sources.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (December 1997), 238 PDF pages
sources.locator: Ch. 2 'Manifolds' printed pp. 50-51 (PDF pp. 57-58): Riemann normal coordinates at a point. Ch. 3 'Curvature' printed pp. 74-76 (PDF pp. 81-83): the commutator of covariant derivatives (3.65)-(3.66), the Riemann tensor (3.67) and its index convention. Printed pp. 79-82 (PDF pp. 86-89): the symmetries (3.78)-(3.83), the Bianchi identity (3.87), the twice-contracted identity (3.94), the Ricci tensor (3.90), the Ricci scalar (3.92) and the Einstein tensor (3.95). Printed pp. 86-88 (PDF pp. 93-95): geodesic deviation (3.110)-(3.113) and its tidal reading. Printed pp. 74-96 (PDF pp. 81-103): the remaining curvature and gravitation material of chapters 3-4.

contents.name: Ch. 3 (3.65)-(3.67): the Riemann tensor defined by the commutator of covariant derivatives, with the index order R^rho_{sigma mu nu}
contents.support: The commutator definition of the curvature operator and the index order of its components are the lecture-notes form restated, in the page's fixed sign convention, by the definition of the curvature operator and components.

contents.name: Ch. 3 (3.90), (3.92), (3.95): the Ricci tensor as a contraction of the Riemann tensor, the Ricci scalar and the Einstein tensor G_{mu nu} = R_{mu nu} - (1/2)R g_{mu nu}
contents.support: The contraction formulas for the Ricci, scalar and Einstein tensors are exactly the derived tensors of the definition's clause (c).

contents.name: Ch. 3 (3.78)-(3.83): the antisymmetries of the lowered Riemann tensor, the exchange of the index pairs and the totally antisymmetric part giving R_{sigma[rho mu nu]} = 0
contents.support: The four displayed identities (3.78)-(3.83) are the source form of clauses (a)-(c) of the algebraic-symmetry theorem.

contents.name: Ch. 3 (3.87): the Bianchi identity R_{mu nu rho sigma;lambda} + R_{mu nu sigma lambda;rho} + R_{mu nu lambda rho;sigma} = 0, and (3.94): its twice-contracted form and the divergence-free Einstein tensor
contents.support: The identity (3.87), its double contraction and the resulting divergence-free property are the source form of the second-Bianchi theorem on this page.

contents.name: Ch. 3 (3.110)-(3.113): the geodesic deviation equation for a family of geodesics, with the relative acceleration given by the Riemann tensor
contents.support: The deviation equation (3.113) between geodesics of a family is the source reading of the theorem's geodesic-deviation clause.

contents.name: Ch. 3 (3.113) closing discussion: the deviation equation read as a tidal acceleration produced by curvature, and the flat-space case with no tidal acceleration
contents.support: The lecture-notes' tidal reading of (3.113), including the vanishing of the relative acceleration when curvature vanishes, is the source of the model-conditional tidal comparison.

contents.name: Ch. 2 'Riemann normal coordinates' and Ch. 3 (3.62)-(3.67): coordinates in which g_{mu nu}(p) = eta_{mu nu} and first derivatives vanish at p, while second derivatives carry the curvature
contents.support: The lecture-notes' first-order normal-coordinate statement supplies the hypothesis of the point-normal four-term formula; the formula itself is proved locally in the theorem's proof.

contents.name: Ch. 3 (3.85) and the curve/curvature discussion: the counting of independent Riemann components (20 in four dimensions) and curvature in one, two and three dimensions
contents.reason: The dimension-specific component counting and the low-dimensional classification are not built on this page; the page uses the four-dimensional algebraic identities and asserts no independent-component count.

contents.name: Ch. 3 (3.95) onwards and Ch. 4 'Gravitation': the Einstein field equation, the Newtonian limit and physics in curved spacetime
contents.reason: The field equation, its coupling and the matter side belong to the Einstein-and-matter page, which also owns the Newtonian and experimental bridges.

sources.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), 126 PDF pages
sources.locator: Chapter 4 'Curvature' printed pp. 40-49 (PDF pp. 41-50): section 4.2 'The Riemann tensor' (4.6)-(4.10), section 4.3 'Parallel transport again' (4.11)-(4.15), section 4.4 'Symmetries of the Riemann tensor' (4.16)-(4.20), section 4.5 'Geodesic deviation' (4.21)-(4.25) and section 4.6 'Curvature of the Levi-Civita connection' (4.26)-(4.35).

contents.name: Section 4.2 'The Riemann tensor' (4.6)-(4.10): the component definition R^mu_{nu rho sigma} and the index convention from the parallel-transport commutator
contents.support: The tensor and component definition (4.6) is restated, in the page's sign convention, by the curvature definition; the batch items cite the convention explicitly.

contents.name: Section 4.3 'Parallel transport again' (4.11)-(4.15): the loop computation Delta Z = R^mu_{nu rho sigma} Z^nu X^rho Y^sigma delta s delta t, expressing curvature as the path dependence of parallel transport
contents.support: The loop form of the curvature operator is absorbed as the geometric motivation of the definition; no separate item is built for it because the component definition is equivalent.

contents.name: Section 4.4 (4.16)-(4.17): the antisymmetry R^a_{b(cd)} = 0 and the first Bianchi identity R^a_{[bcd]} = 0 for a torsion-free connection, with the normal-coordinate proof
contents.support: The normal-coordinate proof of (4.17) is the model for the proof strategy of the algebraic-symmetry theorem, restricted here to the metric-selected connection.

contents.name: Section 4.4 (4.18)-(4.20): the second Bianchi identity R^a_{b[cd;e]} = 0 for a torsion-free connection, with the normal-coordinate derivative computation
contents.support: The identity (4.18) and its coordinate proof are the source of the second-Bianchi theorem; the contracted form is Reall (4.33)-(4.34).

contents.name: Section 4.5 (4.21)-(4.24): one-parameter families of geodesics, the deviation vector S, and the geodesic deviation equation nabla_T nabla_T S = R(T,S)T
contents.support: The derivation of (4.22) through the bracket identity [S,T] = 0 is the source argument behind the commutator and deviation clauses of the theorem.

contents.name: Section 4.5 remark 1: the relative acceleration vanishes for all families of geodesics if and only if the connection is flat
contents.support: The geometric flatness criterion is absorbed into the algebraic vanishing lemma, which proves the pointwise statement for every timelike direction used by the model.

contents.name: Section 4.5 remark 2: geodesic deviation is the tendency of freely falling particles to move apart, corresponding to tidal forces, and the Riemann tensor measures them
contents.support: The tidal reading of the deviation equation is the source of the model-conditional tidal comparison; the item states the assumption structure that the lecture notes leave implicit.

contents.name: Section 4.6 (4.26)-(4.30): the exchange R_{abcd} = R_{cdab}, the trace-free part R_{(ab)cd} = 0 and the symmetry of the Ricci tensor
contents.support: Identities (4.26) and (4.30) are the source form of the pair-exchange and Ricci-symmetry clauses.

contents.name: Section 4.6 (4.29): the four-term normal-coordinate formula R_{mu nu rho sigma} = (1/2)(g_{mu sigma,nu rho} + g_{nu rho,mu sigma} - g_{nu sigma,mu rho} - g_{mu rho,nu sigma}), and (4.35): g_{mu nu} = eta_{mu nu} - (1/3) R_{mu rho nu sigma} X^rho X^sigma + O(X^3)
contents.support: The four-term formula (4.29) is proved as the theorem's point-normal clause; the second-order expansion (4.35) is the source of the example showing that curvature survives the first-order normal form.

contents.name: Section 4.6 (4.31)-(4.34): the Ricci scalar, the Einstein tensor and the contracted Bianchi identity nabla^a G_{ab} = 0, equivalently nabla^a R_{ab} = (1/2) nabla_b R
contents.support: Definitions (4.31)-(4.32) and the contracted identity (4.33)-(4.34) are the source of the divergence-free conclusion of the second-Bianchi theorem.

sources.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), 290 PDF pages
sources.locator: Section 3.2.2 'Torsion and Curvature' printed pp. 105-108 (PDF pp. 112-115): the curvature operator (3.14) and the Riemann tensor (3.15), and the curvature of S^2 in (theta, phi) coordinates (3.20). Section 3.3.2 'Normal Coordinates' printed pp. 119-121 (PDF pp. 126-128): the straight-line geodesics and the counting argument for the second derivatives. Section 3.3.4 'Geodesic Deviation' printed pp. 127-129 (PDF pp. 134-136): the deviation equation (3.36) and the meridian separation of the sphere (3.37)-(3.38). Section 3.4 'More on the Riemann Tensor and its Friends' printed pp. 130-132 (PDF pp. 137-139): the coordinate formula (3.39), the symmetries and the Bianchi identity (3.40), and the Ricci and Einstein tensors (3.4.1).

contents.name: Section 3.2.2 (3.14)-(3.15): the curvature operator R^sigma_{rho mu nu} with the stated sign convention and the Riemann tensor components
contents.support: The lecture-notes convention (3.14)-(3.15) is one of the two independent restatements of the curvature operator used by the definition; the page fixes its own sign and matches the component order to it.

contents.name: Section 3.2.2 (3.20): the curvature of the round S^2 computed from its Christoffel symbols in (theta, phi) coordinates
contents.support: The S^2 computation (3.20) is the source of the worked curvature data of the sphere-factor example, which extends it to the full Lorentzian product and its Ricci, scalar and Einstein tensors.

contents.name: Section 3.3.2 'Normal Coordinates': geodesics through p as straight coordinate lines with g_{mu nu}(p) = eta_{mu nu}, vanishing first derivatives, and the counting argument that second derivatives cannot all be removed
contents.support: The straight-line normal-coordinate construction and the second-derivative counting are the source behind the point-normal clause, whose four-term formula makes the surviving second-order information explicit.

contents.name: Section 3.3.4 (3.36)-(3.38): the geodesic deviation equation and the exact meridian separation s(tau) = r phi sin(v tau) of the sphere, with R^phi_{theta theta phi} = -1
contents.support: The meridian deviation of the sphere, including the vanishing of the separation at tau = pi/v, is the source pattern of the explicit Jacobi field and conjugate instant computed in the equator example.

contents.name: Section 3.4 (3.39): the coordinate formula R^sigma_{rho mu nu} = partial_mu Gamma^sigma_{nu rho} - partial_nu Gamma^sigma_{mu rho} + Gamma^lambda_{nu rho} Gamma^sigma_{mu lambda} - Gamma^lambda_{mu rho} Gamma^sigma_{nu lambda}
contents.support: Formula (3.39) is the source of the chart formula clause of the tensoriality theorem, converted to the page's index order and sign conventions.

contents.name: Section 3.4: the symmetries of the lowered Riemann tensor and the first Bianchi identity R_{sigma[rho mu nu]} = 0 (3.40)
contents.support: The symmety list and (3.40) are a second independent statement of the identities proved by the algebraic-symmetry theorem.

contents.name: Section 3.4.1 'The Ricci and Einstein Tensors': the contractions defining the Ricci tensor, the Ricci scalar and the Einstein tensor
contents.support: The contraction definitions of the Ricci and Einstein tensors are the second treatment of the derived tensors of the definition.

contents.name: Section 3.4.2 'Connection 1-forms and Curvature 2-forms': the tetrad formalism for curvature
contents.reason: The orthonormal-frame and differential-form formalism is not used by this page, whose items are stated in coordinate components and in invariant operator form.

contents.name: Section 3.4.3 'An Example: the Schwarzschild Metric' and chapter 4: the Einstein equations and the Schwarzschild solution
contents.reason: The Schwarzschild curvature computation and the Einstein equations belong to the spherical-vacuum-model page, which owns the vacuum solution and its curvature data.
